title: XACML 3.0
heading: XACML 3.0
lead: This service is a Policy Decision Point. Policies live in ou=policies in the embedded directory — that container is the repository rather than a copy of one — and the Policy Information Point reads attributes off the subject’s own directory entry.
repositoryRoot: The repository holds {policies} policy(ies), {enabled} enabled, and the root is {root}.
repositoryNoRoot: The repository holds {policies} policy(ies), {enabled} enabled, and the root is not set, so every decision is NotApplicable.
enforced: Every endpoint above requires a client certificate this service verifies against an anchor in its own truststore ({door}). The subject DN is resolved to a directory entry, and that entry’s group membership is what grants the role in the last column: {userGroup} grants XACML_USER and {pepGroup} grants REMOTE_PEPS. The certificate says who and the group says whether — a perfectly valid certificate for a common name in neither group is fully authenticated and still refused.
notEnforced: Access enforcement is off (xacml.enforceAccess), so every endpoint above answers without a credential. The roles in the last column are what would be required with it on.
remoteOn: A Policy Enforcement Point in another process registers at /xacml/pep/register, pulls the enabled policies from /xacml/pep/policies and evaluates them itself with its own copy of this engine. {registered} registered. The repository’s sync token is {syncToken}; pass it as ?since= and an unchanged repository answers 304.
remoteOff: Remote Policy Enforcement Points are off (xacml.remotePeps); those three endpoints answer 501.
pip: The Policy Information Point, over HTTP
pipWhy: A remote PEP holds the engine but not the directory, so a designator the request did not carry resolves to an empty bag out there and to a real value here — the same policy deciding two ways in two enforcement points. POST /xacml/pip closes that.
pipShape: XACML defines no PIP protocol, so this invents as little as possible: both directions are XACML’s own XML. Send a {pipRequest} carrying the {request} you are deciding — which is what names the subject — and one {designator} per attribute wanted. What comes back is {attributes} in the shape a {request} carries them, so a PEP splices it into its own request and evaluates — after which its engine finds the values where a designator looks for them, which is exactly what happens in this process when the embedded PDP asks the embedded PIP.
pipUnresolved: An unresolved designator comes back as an absent {attribute} rather than an empty one: that is what a request that never carried it looks like, so a PEP needs no branch for it. MustBePresent is read and deliberately not applied — what an empty bag means is settled by the designator and the function it is handed to, both in your engine. The five reasons a bag can be empty come back in {unresolved}, in this service’s own namespace so that a PEP reading only the XACML core namespace never sees it.
pipPull: The pull is the contract. When the repository changes this service also POSTs a few bytes to each registered PEP that gave a notify URL, saying only that something changed — an optimisation over the polling interval and never a replacement for it, so a PEP that is never nudged still converges.
